models.title: Inventory net realisable value
models.summary: Net realisable value deducts completion and necessary selling costs from the ordinary-course estimated selling price.

relationship.original_equation: Net realisable value = estimated selling price - completion costs - selling costs
relationship.locator: About: net realisable value and measurement
relationship.translation_notes: Inputs are total monetary amounts for one explicitly identified scope; negative calculated NRV is not clamped.

models.title: LIFO liquidation gross-profit effect for one cost layer
models.summary: The example computes the gross-profit difference for liquidated old-layer units against current replacement cost.

relationship.original_equation: Gross profit from liquidation = units liquidated × (current replacement cost per unit - historical layer cost per unit)
relationship.translation_notes: The unit count is dimensionless; both monetary inputs are currency per same item and the output is total currency.

variables.definition: Count of identical units released from the specified older layer

Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: All released units are from a homogeneous cost layer and share the stated replacement cost.
The comparison holds sales volume and price constant and isolates the accounting cost difference.
limitations: The result is a relative pretax gross-profit effect, not a cash flow or proof of operational improvement.
Multiple layers or replacement costs require separate effects to be summed.
